id.description: ID is its tag path and name, e.g. "projects/acme/standup".

kind.description:
Kind is what installing it adds: a routine (an LLM routine), a
program, a hook or a watcher.

project.description:
Project is the project it's for (its folder under projects/, e.g.
"acme"); empty for every project or none.

backends.description: Backends it works with (llm.backend values); none: any.

required.description:
Required is true for a parameter without a default; DefaultText is the
default written as `templates install --set` takes it. Both are worked
out when the routine is parsed.

command.description:
Command is run with its first word looked up on my PATH; one argument
holds OutputPlaceholder, where the executable must be written.

dir.description:
Dir is the folder it runs in, relative to the template's (its source,
within the templates folder, e.g. one several templates share): it's
copied to a temporary folder first. Default: the template's own.

build.description:
Build is how its executable is built when it's installed (a program's,
a hook's or a watcher's that ships as source).

watcher.description:
Watcher is a hook's: the watcher it listens to, installed with it (from
its template) when it isn't there.

runsHere.description: RunsHere is false for templates for another OS (listed with --all).

supportsBackend.description:
SupportsBackend is false for a template that doesn't work with the
selected backend (llm.backend): installing it is refused.

installed.description:
Installed is true when one of its kind with the template's name exists
(a routine of either kind, a hook, a watcher).

required.description:
Required is true for a parameter without a default; DefaultText is the
default written as `templates install --set` takes it. Both are worked
out when the routine is parsed.

installed.description:
Installed is true when the watcher is there already: installing the
hook then uses it.

withWatcher.description:
WithWatcher is a hook template's watcher template: installing the hook
installs it too while it isn't installed, so the two are one choice.
Its parameters are among the hook's (params) while it isn't
installed. A watcher template a hook comes with isn't listed on its
own.

items.description: TemplateInfo is one row of `templates list --json`.
